::: {.why}
The trading rule should fall out of the estimated dynamics rather than out of a parameter sweep, and this is the one case this year where that is genuinely possible.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Estimate a spread's mean reversion speed, convert it to a half-life in days, and attach a standard error to it.
- Derive entry and exit thresholds from the fitted stationary distribution, and report the parameter surface around them rather than the peak.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Derive the link rather than quoting it: regressing the spread change on its lagged level gives a coefficient that maps to the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck reversion speed, and the half-life is the log of two over that speed. Estimate it with a standard error for every selected pair, and exclude any pair whose half-life exceeds a fifth of the formation window, because that estimate is not identified.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Set the thresholds from the model: the fitted stationary standard deviation gives the natural scale, so entry at two of those and exit at zero is derived rather than chosen. Implement it in qlib/signals/pairs.py.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Map the surface anyway and report it: entry from 1.0 to 3.0, exit from minus 0.5 to 1.0, Sharpe plotted as a surface with your derived point marked. A flat surface means the rule is robust; a sharp peak elsewhere is the thing to distrust. Every point logs to research_log.jsonl.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The pairs rule takes its holding period and its thresholds from the fitted mean-reversion dynamics, and the parameter surface around that point is reported rather than hidden. Every point on the surface is a logged trial, which keeps the trial count honest.
:::

## Resources

- [Avellaneda & Lee (2010) — Statistical arbitrage in the US equities market](https://traders.studentorg.berkeley.edu/papers/Statistical%20arbitrage%20in%20the%20US%20equities%20market.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}
- [Carr & López de Prado (2014) — Determining Optimal Trading Rules without Backtesting](https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.1159) [paper]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
Half-life estimates with standard errors per pair, an exclusion rule for the unidentified ones, and the Sharpe surface with the derived point marked.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Given an estimated half-life of 12 days, what holding period does that imply, and what goes wrong if the true half-life is 60?
:::
